people.name: Ben Darvill

people.name: Cait O'Riordan
people.description: Cait O'Riordan, from Irish-British Celtic punk band The Pogues who scored the 1987 UK No.8 single 'The Irish Rover' and the 1987 UK No.2 single with Kirsty MaCcoll, 'Fairytale Of New York'.

people.name: David Glasper
people.description: David Glasper, singer from English pop band Breathe, who had the 1988 UK No.4 and US No.2 single 'Hands To Heaven'.

people.name: Martin Mcaloon
people.description: Martin Mcaloon, bassist from English English pop band Prefab Sprout who had the 1988 UK No.7 single 'The King Of Rock 'n' Roll'.

people.name: Robin Guthrie
people.description: Scottish musician, songwriter Robin Guthrie, from Cocteau Twins. The group released the album Heaven or Las Vegas in late 1990 which became the most commercially successful of their many recordings.

people.name: Till Lindemann
people.description: Till Lindemann poet, lead vocalist for the German rock band Rammstein who formed in Berlin in 1994. Five of their albums reached No.1 on the German album charts.

people.name: Michael Stipe
people.description: Michael Stipe, American singer, songwriter, musician, from R.E.M., who were pivotal in the creation and development of the alternative rock genre. He formed R.E.M. after meeting his bandmates at University in Georgia in Athens, and soon dropped out to pursue music with them. The band issued its debut single, 'Radio Free Europe' (1981) and subsequently signed to I.R.S. Records, meeting wide acclaim and soon great commercial success. They had the 1991 UK No.6 & US No.10 single 'Shiny Happy People', plus over 20 Top 40 UK singles and the 1992 UK No.1 & US No.2 album Automatic For The People.

people.name: Lorna Doom
people.description: American musician Lorna Doom. She was the bass guitarist for the punk rock band the Germs. Their music was influential to many later punk rock acts. Germs guitarist Pat Smear went on to achieve greater fame performing with Nirvana and Foo Fighters. Doom died on 16 January 2019 of cancer age 61.

people.name: Macel King
people.description: Macel King, singer from British soul group Sweet Sensation who scored the 1974 UK No.1 and US No.14 single 'Sad Sweet Dreamer'.

people.name: Nels Cline
people.description: Nels Cline, guitarist from American alternative rock band Wilco who released the albums Yankee Hotel Foxtrot, A Ghost Is Born, Sky Blue Sky and Wilco (The Album).

people.name: Bernard Sumner
people.description: Bernard Sumner, the founding member of the bands Joy Division, New Order, Electronic, and Bad Lieutenant. Sumner was an early force in several areas, including the post-punk, synth-pop, and techno music scenes. Joy Division had the 1980 UK No.13 single 'Love Will Tear Us Apart' and New Order had the 1983 UK No.9 single 'Blue Monday' and with Electronic, (with Johnny Marr), the 1991 UK No.8 single 'Get The Message'.

people.name: Brian Ray
people.description: American session musician, guitarist, bassist, singer–songwriter and musical director, Brian Ray, best known for his work as a rhythm guitarist and bassist with Paul McCartney.

people.name: Clive Gregson
people.description: English singer, songwriter, musician and record producer Clive Gregson. He was the leader of late 70s Stiff Records band Any Trouble, and later one half of folk duo Gregson & Collister. He worked on several records with Richard Thompson and was part of his touring band. His songs have been covered by Kim Carnes, Norma Waterson, Jimmy Buffett and Nanci Griffith. Gregson is now a member of The Guilty Men.

people.name: Mark Hollis
people.description: Mark Hollis, English musician and singer-songwriter. He achieved commercial success and critical acclaim in the 1980s and 1990s as the co-founder, lead singer and principal songwriter of the band Talk Talk. Hollis wrote or co-wrote most of Talk Talk's music, including hits like 'It's My Life' (1984) and 'Life's What You Make It' (1986). He died aged 64 on 25 February 2019.

people.name: Arthur Conley
people.description: Arthur Conley, US soul singer, known for the 1967 US No.2 & UK No.7 single 'Sweet Soul Music. He first recorded in 1959 as the lead singer of Arthur & the Corvets. Conley died of cancer on 17th November 2003.

people.name: John McLaughlin
people.description: British guitarist John McLaughlin, who formed the Mahavishnu Orchestra and has also worked with Carlos Santana, Stanley Clark and Jaco Pastorius. Prior to the Mahavishnu Orchestra, in the 1960s, he played with Alexis Korner, Georgie Fame and the Blue Flames, the Graham Bond Organisation and Brian Auger. In 1969 he moved to New York to join Tony Williams' Lifetime. On March 25th of that year he jammed with Jimi Hendrix at the Record Plant, recalling ‘we played from 2 until 8 in the morning. In 2010, Jeff Beck called McLaughlin ‘the best guitarist alive’.

people.name: John Gorman
people.description: John Gorman, singer, with the comedy, poetry and music trio The Scaffold. They are best known for their 1967 hit 'Thank U Very Much' and the 1968 Christmas UK No.1 single 'Lily The Pink'.

people.name: William 'Mickey' Stevenson
people.description: American songwriter and record producer William 'Mickey' Stevenson. He was head of the Motown A&R department in the mid-1960s and was responsible for organizing the company's in-house studio band, which came to be known as the Funk Brothers.

people.name: Don Arden
people.description: English music manager, agent, and businessman Don Arden. He managed the careers of rock acts such as Jerry Lee Lewis, Little Richard, Gene Vincent, Small Faces, The Move, Black Sabbath, and Electric Light Orchestra. Arden gained a reputation in Britain for his aggressive, sometimes illegal business tactics, which led to his being called "Mr Big", the "English Godfather", and the "Al Capone of Pop". Arden is the father of Sharon Osbourne. He died in Los Angeles on 21 July 2007.

works.title: Silver Lady
works.eventDescription: American-British actor and singer David Soul died age 80. Soul was a three-pack-a-day cigarette smoker for 50 years and was seriously affected by COPD and had also had a lung removed due to cancer. He was known for his role as Detective Kenneth "Hutch" Hutchinson in the television series Starsky & Hutch from 1975 to 1979 and had the 1976 UK No.1 'Silver Lady' and the 1977 UK & US No.1 single 'Don't Give Up On Us'.

works.title: Hackney Diamonds
works.eventDescription: The biggest-selling vinyl album of 2023 by a British act was Rolling Stones' Hackney Diamonds. Released in October 2023, it became the Stones’ 14th No.1 album and enjoyed a second week at the top as 2023’s Official Christmas No. 1 album. The first album of original material by the Rolling Stones since 2005's A Bigger Bang, Hackney Diamonds reached No.1 in 20 countries and features guest contributions from Elton John, Lady Gaga, Paul McCartney, Stevie Wonder, and former Rolling Stones bassist Bill Wyman.

works.title: We Can't Stop
works.eventDescription: Miley Cyrus settled the $300 million copyright infringement lawsuit that accused the singer of stealing her 2013 hit 'We Can’t Stop.' The lawsuit, filed in 2018, was made by Jamaican songwriter Michael May, who alleged that 'We Can’t Stop' replicated his 1988 track 'We Run Things.'

works.title: Baby Boy
works.eventDescription: Beyoncé won a long-running legal wrangle over claims her hit song 'Baby Boy' infringed the copyright of another artist's work. The appeals court in Houston, Texas upheld a 2006 decision which dismissed musician Jennifer Armour's claims that its lyrics were based on her work. Ms Armour claimed she had posted 'I Got A Little Bit Of Love For You' to Beyonce's manager and record company in early 2003.

works.title: Slim Shady
works.eventDescription: The owner of a recording studio where Eminem recorded his 'Slim Shady' LP was found shot dead. AJ Abdallah, who was 36, was discovered by a business colleague at the Detroit studio, it was thought he had been dead for at least two days. Police suggested that a robbery may also have taken place. Mr Abdallah had lived in a apartment above the studio on Eight Mile Road, the Detroit street which inspired the title of Eminem's 2002 film '8 Mile.'

works.title: Whiskey in the Jar
works.eventDescription: Irish singer, songwriter and bassist Phil Lynott of Thin Lizzy died of heart failure and pneumonia after being in a coma for eight days following a drug overdose. With Thin Lizzy he had the 1973 hit 'Whiskey in the Jar', (their version of the traditional Irish song) and hits with ‘The Boys Are Back in Town’, ‘Jailbreak’ and ‘Waiting for an Alibi’. The groups 1978 album 'Live and Dangerous' spent 62 weeks on the UK chart. Lynott fronted several bands as a lead vocalist, including Skid Row alongside Gary Moore. A life-size bronze statue of Phil Lynott was unveiled on Harry Street in Dublin Ireland in 2005.

works.title: Let It Be
works.eventDescription: The Beatles (without John Lennon) re-record vocals and a new guitar solo on the Paul McCartney song 'Let It Be' at Studio Two, EMI Studios, London. This session will be the final studio appearance for The Beatles, as a group. (The final date that all four of The Beatles were in the studio together is August 20, 1969).

works.title: Light My Fire

The album features their breakthrough single 'Light My Fire' and the lengthy song 'The End' with its Oedipal spoken word section. The album was recorded at Sunset Sound Studios in Hollywood, California over six days and unique packaging of the album included each band members bio.
